title: The digital era
topic: how students use digital tools
task_meta: Vocabulary : terminology related to the digital era, definitions, general vocabulary
grammar_rules:
Subject + Verb + Object (Word order (so‘z tartibi), Positive / Negative / Question)

Word Order — Ingliz tilida so‘z tartibi

Siz bilan ingliz tilida gap tuzishni o‘rganamiz. Ingliz tilida gap tuzishda eng muhim narsalardan biri bu so‘z tartibi. O‘zbek tilida so‘zlarning joyi biroz erkinroq bo‘lishi mumkin, lekin ingliz tilida gapdagi so‘zlar aniq tartibda keladi. Masalan, o‘zbek tilida “Men ingliz tilini o‘rganaman” deymiz. Ingliz tilida esa bu gap I study English bo‘ladi. Ya’ni ingliz tilida odatda avval kim?, keyin nima qiladi?, undan keyin nimani? keladi. Shuning uchun inglizcha gap tuzishda eng asosiy formula:

Subject + Verb + Object, ya’ni Ega + Fe’l + To‘ldiruvchi.

Bu mavzu kundalik hayotda juda ko‘p ishlatiladi. Siz o‘zingiz haqingizda gapirmoqchi bo‘lsangiz, do‘stingizni tanishtirsangiz, nimani yoqtirishingizni aytsangiz yoki biror ish-harakatni tushuntirsangiz, word order kerak bo‘ladi. Masalan: I like music — “Men musiqani yoqtiraman”, She reads books — “U kitoblar o‘qiydi”, They play football — “Ular futbol o‘ynaydi”. Bu gaplarda tartib bir xil: avval subject, keyin verb, keyin object kelgan.

Ingliz tilida oddiy darak gaplarda ko‘pincha formula shunday bo‘ladi: Subject + Verb + Object. Masalan, I watch movies, We learn English, Ali plays chess. Bu gaplarda I, we, Ali — subject, watch, learn, plays — verb, movies, English, chess — object. O‘zbek talabalari ko‘p qiladigan xato shuki, ular o‘zbekcha tartibni inglizchaga ko‘chiradi. Masalan, I English learn deyishadi. Bu noto‘g‘ri. To‘g‘ri shakli: I learn English.

grammar_rules:
Ingliz tilida pronoun, ya’ni olmosh, otning o‘rnida ishlatiladigan so‘zdir. Masalan, har safar Ali, Ali, Ali deb takrorlash o‘rniga, biz he deymiz. This is Ali. Ali is my friend. Ali is a student deyish o‘rniga, tabiiyroq qilib: This is Ali. He is my friend. He is a student deymiz. Demak, olmoshlar gapni qisqaroq, chiroyliroq va takrorsiz qilish uchun kerak. Ingliz tilida olmoshlar juda muhim, chunki ular gapda kim haqida gap ketayotganini, narsa kimga tegishli ekanini yoki ish-harakat kimning o‘ziga qaratilganini bildiradi. Eng ko‘p ishlatiladigan olmosh turlari: personal pronouns — kishilik olmoshlari, possessive pronouns / possessive adjectives — egalik olmoshlari va reflexive pronouns — o‘zlik olmoshlaridir.

Personal pronouns, ya’ni kishilik olmoshlari, shaxs yoki narsani bildiradi. Ular gapda ega yoki to‘ldiruvchi bo‘lib kelishi mumkin. Ega bo‘lib kelganda: I, you, he, she, it, we, they ishlatiladi. Masalan:

I am a student — Men talabaman. You are my friend — Sen mening do‘stimsan. He is a teacher — U erkak kishi o‘qituvchi. She is a doctor — U ayol kishi shifokor. It is a book — Bu kitob. We are students — Biz talabamiz. They are teachers — Ular o‘qituvchilar.

Bu yerda olmoshlar gapning boshida kelib, ish-harakatni bajarayotgan shaxs yoki narsani bildiradi. Ingliz tilida he erkak kishi uchun, she ayol kishi uchun, it esa hayvon, narsa, predmet yoki mavhum tushunchalar uchun ishlatiladi. Masalan: This is my phone. It is new — Bu mening telefonim. U yangi.

grammar_rules:
Noun (ot) – sanaladigan / sanalmaydigan (Countable vs Uncountable nouns)

Ingliz tilida noun, ya’ni ot, odam, narsa, joy, hayvon, fikr yoki tushunchaning nomini bildiradi: student, book, water, idea, school, happiness. Otlar ingliz tilida ikki katta guruhga bo‘linadi: countable nouns va uncountable nouns.

Countable nouns — bu sanash mumkin bo‘lgan otlar. Ya’ni ularning bittasini, ikkitasini, uchtasini alohida sanay olamiz. Masalan:

one book, two books, three students, five apples.

Bunday otlarning singular va plural shakli bo‘ladi. Bitta bo‘lsa oldidan ko‘pincha a/an ishlatiladi: a book, an apple, a student. Ko‘plikda esa odatda -s / -es qo‘shiladi: books, apples, boxes, buses. Masalan:

I have a book — “Menda bitta kitob bor”. She bought three apples — “U uchta olma sotib oldi”.

Bu yerda book va apple sanaladi, chunki ularni donalab hisoblash mumkin.

Uncountable nouns esa sanab bo‘lmaydigan otlardir. Ular odatda suyuqlik, kukun, modda, ovqat nomlari, umumiy tushuncha yoki hissiyotlarni bildiradi. Masalan:

a good student — yaxshi talaba, a red car — qizil mashina, a new phone — yangi telefon, a small room — kichik xona.

Students connect a keyboard, mouse, printer and external drive to a desktop computer. The teacher asks them to follow the steps in the correct order so that no device is damaged.

reading_passage:
This week I learned about daily life in Great Britain. Our class used a realistic situation from a student exchange blog.

Leo stays with a host family in Manchester and travels to university by tram. His host father drinks tea every morning while Leo usually chooses coffee.

Shops in the neighbourhood close earlier on Sunday than on other days. Leo studies in the library after classes and calls his family every evening.

One sentence in the lesson shows the grammar in context: “Amina usually studies in the evening and often checks messages after class.” The routine becomes familiar after his first two weeks in Britain.

The text gives students useful vocabulary from the topic. It also asks them to notice details, not only individual words. After reading, Amina explains the main idea to Tom and supports the answer with information from the text.

The final task asks readers to connect the topic with their own experience. They should explain one idea in their own words and then use the lesson grammar in a new sentence about daily life in Great Britain.

grammar_rules:
Adverb (ravish)

Ingliz tilida adverb, ya’ni ravish, ish-harakatning qanday, qachon, qayerda, qanchalik darajada yoki necha marta bajarilishini bildiradi. Oddiy qilib aytganda, adverb fe’l haqida qo‘shimcha ma’lumot beradi. Masalan, He speaks — “U gapiradi” degani. Lekin He speaks clearly desak, “U aniq gapiradi” degan ma’no chiqadi. Bu yerda clearly ravish bo‘lib, u gapirish harakati qanday bajarilayotganini ko‘rsatadi. Yana bir misol:

She runs fast — U tez yuguradi. They arrived yesterday — Ular kecha yetib kelishdi. We study here — Biz shu yerda o‘qiymiz.

Bu gaplarda fast, yesterday, here so‘zlari ravish vazifasida kelgan.

Adverb ko‘pincha “qanday?” degan savolga javob beradi. Bunday ravishlar odatda sifatga -ly qo‘shimchasini qo‘shish orqali yasaladi:

slow — slowly, quick — quickly, careful — carefully, beautiful — beautifully, clear — clearly.

Masalan: He drives carefully — U ehtiyotkorlik bilan mashina haydaydi. She answered quickly — U tez javob berdi. The teacher explained the topic clearly — O‘qituvchi mavzuni aniq tushuntirdi.

Bu yerda ravishlar ish-harakatning qanday tarzda bajarilganini bildiradi. Sifat odam yoki narsani tasvirlasa, ravish harakatni tasvirlaydi. Masalan: He is a careful driver — U ehtiyotkor haydovchi. Bu gapda careful sifat, chunki driver otini tasvirlayapti. He drives carefully — U ehtiyotkorlik bilan haydaydi. Bu gapda esa carefully ravish, chunki drives fe’lini tasvirlayapti.

One sentence in the lesson shows the grammar in context: “Eva works carefully and usually finishes on time.” The seminar concludes that remote work is useful when teams manage communication well.

The text gives students useful vocabulary from the topic. It also asks them to notice details, not only individual words. After reading, Eva explains the main idea to Noah and supports the answer with information from the text.

The final task asks readers to connect the topic with their own experience. They should explain one idea in their own words and then use the lesson grammar in a new sentence about the growth of remote work.

grammar_rules:
Preposition (predloglar)

Ingliz tilida preposition, ya’ni predlog, so‘zlar orasidagi munosabatni bildiradigan yordamchi so‘zdir. Predloglar odatda ot, olmosh yoki joy nomlari bilan birga ishlatiladi va biror narsa qayerda, qachon, qaysi tomonga, nima bilan yoki kim haqida ekanini ko‘rsatadi. O‘zbek tilida bunday ma’nolar ko‘pincha qo‘shimchalar orqali beriladi: “uyda”, “maktabga”, “darsdan keyin”, “do‘stim bilan”. Ingliz tilida esa bu ma’nolar alohida so‘zlar bilan ifodalanadi: in the house, to school, after the lesson, with my friend. Shuning uchun predloglar ingliz tilida juda muhim, chunki ular gapning ma’nosini aniq qiladi.

Eng ko‘p ishlatiladigan predloglardan biri in bo‘lib, u odatda “ichida”, “da” degan ma’noni beradi. Masalan: in the room— xonada, in the bag — sumkaning ichida, in Uzbekistan — O‘zbekistonda, in 2026 — 2026-yilda. In biror narsaning ichida, chegaralangan joyda yoki katta vaqt oralig‘ida ishlatiladi. Masalan: I am in the classroom — Men sinfxonadaman. There is a book in my bag — Sumkamda kitob bor. He was born in 2010 — U 2010-yilda tug‘ilgan. Bu yerda in joy yoki vaqt ichida bo‘lish ma’nosini beradi.

On predlogi odatda “ustida”, “da” degan ma’noni beradi. U biror narsa yuzaning ustida turganini bildiradi. Masalan: on the table — stol ustida, on the wall — devorda, on the floor — polda. Gaplarda: The book is on the table — Kitob stol ustida. There is a picture on the wall — Devorda rasm bor. On vaqt bilan ham ishlatiladi, ayniqsa hafta kunlari va aniq sanalarda: on Monday — dushanba kuni, on May 23 — 23-may kuni, on my birthday — tug‘ilgan kunimda. Masalan: We have English on Monday — Bizda dushanba kuni ingliz tili bor.

The student magazine has a new feature on different types of computer software. It begins with a situation from an introductory computing lecture.

System software controls the basic operation of a computer while application software helps users complete specific tasks. A computer may contain many applications but only a few programs are used every day.

listening_transcript:
Amina: Tom, I was thinking about our lesson on protecting a national cultural treasure.
Tom: Me too. We have to present final recommendations for protecting a heritage site, so the details matter.
Amina: I wrote down the first point. Tell me if this is right.
Tom: Amina says visitor numbers should be controlled during the busiest months.
Amina: What did you write for the next point?
Tom: Tom recommends training local guides to explain why some areas are restricted.
Amina: I nearly missed another detail.
Tom: They agree that tourism income should support conservation work.
Amina: Yes, and there is one more fact we should not forget.
Tom: Amina concludes that protection will succeed only if residents are included in decisions.
Amina: Let’s check the grammar before we finish.
Tom: For example: In conclusion, protecting cultural heritage requires both public responsibility and long-term planning.
Amina: Great. What happened in the end?
Tom: Their final recommendation balances education, access and preservation.
